<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with clean, closed-book-appropriate evidence (cocoa value chain, Botswana, Ajaokuta, East Asian sequencing) and no fake precision. CON won because it imposed the decision rule that organized the whole debate — the word "over" means either nothing (slogan) or it means real diversion from the sector that earns foreign exchange (self-harm) — and it made that dilemma bite in stages. PRO deserves credit for meeting the dilemma honestly in Rebuttal 2 by naming actual teeth (differential export duties, allocating the marginal megawatt and rail capital, forgone customs revenue), which was the most impressive single move of the debate. But CON then converted that disclosure into concrete harm (lower farmgate prices, cross-border smuggling toward the better price, taxing the FX earner to subsidize a processor that cannot yet compete), and PRO's closing answered only at the level of weighing ("certainly unable to hire") rather than rebutting the mechanism. CON also won the geometry clash: PRO's concession that "Africa has no rich neighbour, so the market must be built" was a real cost, and CON's reply — purchasing power cannot be decreed by treaty, so the market is absent on the day the megawatt moves — was left standing. PRO's best live route, the demographic/jobs argument anchored in Botswana, genuinely damaged CON's "it's a governance problem, not a product problem" framing, and CON never fully explained where its jobs come from beyond assertion; that keeps this competitive rather than lopsided. But CON answered Botswana coherently twice (diversification is slow even under ideal conditions, hence fund it from strength), whereas PRO's claim that the composition and Botswana points went "never answered" was overstated given B2.5 and B2.7. Minor execution cost to CON for the clipped over-length Rebuttal 2, though little substance was lost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 response to PRO's newly disclosed "teeth": accepting the win-win instruments while showing that the actual ranking-bearing tools (export duties on raw beans, denied mine connections, pulled rail money) tax the farmer and the foreign-exchange earner and invite smuggling — turning PRO's honest concession into the case against the motion's word "over."</best_rebuttal>
